prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the edit target: the previous Myth two-tone ink Taiji wave logo.
Make ONE revised logo. First rotate the existing composition 180 degrees, then carefully recompose its central Taiji fish. Exactly TWO fish eyes, opposite colors, must have their centers on EXACTLY THE SAME HORIZONTAL LINE, side by side with balanced spacing, not diagonal. After rotation the BLACK fish is on the LEFT and the IVORY fish is on the RIGHT. The central dividing S-curve is the origin of the motion: extend its two ends out through the left and right into long, tapered complementary brush waves. Open and pull the inner seam outward; do not simply add wings around a circular yin-yang badge. Two flowing crests and one central valley create a confident wave M silhouette.
Whole mark should feel painted in one fluent Chinese landscape ink / po-mo calligraphic gesture: expressive wet ink masses, controlled dry-brush edges, elegant negative-space flow and fine tapering ends. Keep the compact central mass and the opposite eyes readable. Eyes can have subtle organic painted edges but their centers MUST be horizontally aligned. No hard perfect vector circles except the legibility needed for the two eyes. Flat pigment black #0E100F and opaque ivory #F8F4ED, genuinely transparent background. No scenery, landscape objects, paper background, extraneous splatter cloud, gradients, lighting, 3D, lettering, frame or red seal. Wide tightly framed composition, a refined contemporary art-institution identity, not a decorative stock yin-yang with wings. Preserve transparent alpha and opaque ivory paint.
use: Static Myth identity; tiny waiting Taiji remains a legible geometric micro mark.
